title: Landing Gear
intro: You can't stop, cut or push off a leg that can't take a landing, so this session starts there. You take the force in, then you give it back. If you haven't done any jump work lately, start here, before Off the Mark and Hard Stop. You need trainers or court shoes, about four metres of clear, non-slip floor and nothing overhead you could hit, like a fan, a light or a low beam. A court or a rubber mat is kinder than tile or concrete. You'll also need a line to hop over, like a court line or a strip of tape. Skip the Countermovement Jump if there's something overhead. Skip the Lateral Bound if you don't have four clear metres, or if you've ever torn a knee ligament. Don't add reps to make up for anything you skip. It's about ninety ground contacts in all.

First time through, do about half of the Rebound and Springs blocks and take the full rest. It still counts as a full session. If a landing gets loud or sloppy, end the session there. Keep it 48 hours away from another hard session, and don't do it the day before a match. In a tournament week, skip this and do Green Light from the Mobility list. If you're coming back from an ankle injury, ask whoever treated you if landing and jumping are OK. If you have a sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles right now, or an injury has kept you off court in the last month, this isn't the session for today, so get it looked at first. Stop the session and get it checked if you get a sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop at the back of your thigh, in your groin, your calf or your Achilles. Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right means stop now and get it looked at before you train again. If a doctor has told you to be careful with hard exercise, check with them before you do this one. If you are far more sore than normal a day or two later, or your pee goes dark, get that checked the same day.

good: Jog easy, or march on the spot if you're indoors, until you're warm and breathing a little harder
Feel your legs loosen up with every minute
Drive the knee forward over your toes
Feel the stretch low in the calf and the front of the ankle
bad: Letting the heel lift or the arch collapse

good: Hold a wall and swing the leg front to back, then side to side
Feel the hip loosen up as the swing gets bigger
bad: Arching your lower back to throw the leg higher

good: Step wide and sit back into that hip, chest tall
Feel the inside of the straight leg stretch
bad: Letting the bent knee cave inward

good: Step long, drop the back hip, then reach the inside arm up to the ceiling
Feel the front of the back hip and your upper back open up
bad: Rushing the reach before the hips have dropped

good: Push the floor away through your heels
Feel your glutes squeeze at the top
bad: Arching your lower back to lift higher

good: Rise onto the ball of your foot, pause, then lower slowly
Feel the calf working, not just the toes
From tall on your toes, snap down into an athletic stance and freeze, as quietly as you can
Your hips go back and your knees soak it up
bad: Landing stiff-legged and taking it through your knees

good: From tall on one foot, snap down into a single-leg landing and freeze
Feel your hip and thigh catching the landing, not your knee
bad: Letting your knee cave inward on the landing

good: Dip fast and jump as high as you can
Feel the floor pushing back through your whole foot
Push off one foot and bound sideways as far as you can still land and hold for two seconds
Feel the outside of the landing hip catching you
bad: Letting your landing knee cave inward

good: Stay stiff through the ankles and bounce off the floor quickly
Your calves acting like springs
bad: Landing on your heels instead of the balls of your feet

good: Hop over the line and back as fast as you can, both feet together
Feel your ankles doing the work, with quiet contacts
